items.why: BLOCKER (a). parseParagraph matches PARAGRAPH_RULES against the start of the paragraph and slices the match out of `rest` BEFORE the sentence loop, but `antecedent` is only ever set inside that loop from the sentences that survive. A sentence trailing the template is therefore parsed with antecedent === false, the line-841 `it`/`that creature`/`that permanent` -> `thatobj` rewrite never fires, and the pronoun falls back to the source. On God-Pharaoh's Gift that gave a noncreature Artifact the haste printed for its 4/4 Zombie token (CR 608.2, 110.5). Proven with built-ins only, no registry rule involved: "Create a token that's a copy of target creature. It gains haste until end of turn." -> grant-keyword target 'that' (correct), while "You may sacrifice a creature. If you do, create a token that's a copy of target creature. It gains haste until end of turn." -> grant-keyword target 'self' (wrong). Both are pinned in test/parser-generic-you-do.test.ts; the second assertion is the acceptance test and flips to 'that' when this lands. Note `optional-pay` does NOT show the bug (its Y slot regex `(.+?)\.?$` swallows the trailing sentence into a nested parseEffects, where the antecedent is set normally); only `optional-then`, whose Y slot is `([^.]+)`, leaves the sentence behind in `rest`. NOT VERIFIED END TO END: I could not apply the patch to measure it (editing parse.ts is out of scope for this wave, and the sandbox denied even a temporary probe). Seeding the flag is necessary but may not be sufficient — bindAntecedent/readsFrame/bindsFrame are then handed an `out` whose only member is the `optional-then` wrapper, so they must also look inside its `first`/`then` arrays to find the binding op. Both halves want checking together, then re-run parse:diff.
cards: Sephiroth, Fabled SOLDIER // Sephiroth, One-Winged Angel

items.why: Blocker 603.2 (Dreamborn Muse), confirmed. parseAmountPhrase answers "the number of cards in their hand" / "in that player's hand" / "in target player's hand" with `{count:'cards-in-hand', filter:{other:true}}`, but evalAmount's `case 'cards-in-hand'` is `s.players[ctrl].hand.length` with `ctrl = item.actor ?? item.controller` (src/engine/characteristics.ts:160, src/engine/game.ts:1062) and never reads `filter.other`. With no `scoped` wrapper the amount is the ABILITY CONTROLLER's hand. Verified: seat 0 = Dreamborn Muse + 3 cards in hand, seat 1 = empty hand; on seat 1's upkeep seat 1 milled 3 (library 20 -> 17, graveyard 0 -> 3). Correct result is 0. The amount FORM `{prop:'cards-in-hand', of:'that-player'}` is resolved correctly by evalAmountForm through the binding frame (characteristics.ts:124-127, resolveOnePlayer) and is already what src/cards/rules/composition.ts:260 emits for the same phrase — so this is a one-line built-in correction, not an engine gap. It is still a built-in edit, and it moves five cards already in the pool that carry the same amount and are wrong today (Search Warrant, Sudden Impact, Stormbreath Dragon, Gaze of Adamaro, Storm Seeker), so it belongs in its own wave with its own parse:diff read.
cards: Halvar, God of Battle // Sword of the Realms

items.why: Major 603.3d (Ley Line), confirmed. The scoped rule reduces "that player may put a +1/+1 counter on target creature of their choice" to `scoped(that-player, may(counters target {kind:'creature'}))` — identical to the same sentence without the rider, which is the defect. `scoped` moves `item.actor` at RESOLUTION, but a triggered ability's targets are chosen when it goes on the stack, by `targetOptionsFor(this, t.controller, ...)` / `targetOptionsFor(this, item.controller, ...)` (src/engine/game.ts:2320, 2340). Verified: seat 0 = Ley Line + Grizzly Bears, seat 1 = Runeclaw Bear; on seat 1's upkeep the +1/+1 counter landed on seat 0's Grizzly Bears. Letting the triggering player choose a printed `target` is an engine capability that does not exist (and this wave adds no op), so the minimal safe core change is the guard below: decline the scoped block rather than drop the chooser. Measured cost today: 0 fully-parsed paper cards move (the only triggered `scoped(non-you)` block containing a nested `target` key is Descent into Avernus, whose text contains no printed "target"). The guard is what makes it safe for a later wave to re-claim the "each player's upkeep" head; the real fix — a per-target chooser on a trigger — is an engine feature and a separate plan item.
cards: Halvar, God of Battle // Sword of the Realms

items.why: The leading-pronoun rewrite in parseEffectSentence turns "It" / "That creature" into `~` (the source) for every verb outside its short list, so the registry is offered "~ blocks this turn if able" for Provoke and "~ must be blocked this turn if able" for Enlarge / Vengeant Earth / Disturbed Slumber / King Harald's Revenge / Timely Interference — a rule can never see the antecedent, and claiming the `~` form would put the requirement on the sorcery instead of on the creature it untapped. Adding the combat verbs to the `thatobj` marker list makes the antecedent visible; a registry rule could then emit the exact `{ op: 'blocks-if-able', target: 'that', duration: 'eot' }` for Provoke and Timely Interference (the "must be blocked" cards still need openIssue 3's op as well). The wording is declined here and pinned as a decline in test/parser-generic-able.test.ts.

The construct's meaning is in the sentence AFTER the payment, and only parse.ts ever sees two sentences at once (a registry `EffectRule` is handed one normalised sentence and `EffectCtx` carries no lookahead; a `LineRule` never sees these lines at all, because the line loop's triggered branch at parse.ts:2010 claims them and `continue`s before tryLineRules at parse.ts:2077). Two paragraph templates beside the existing one at parse.ts:624 are what the construct actually needs: "When you do" -> `optional-pay` whose `then` is the `reflexive` (CR 603.12, one prompt, one gate, a shape render.ts already prints), and "If you don't" -> `unless-pays` (CR 118.12), which carries the cost AND the mandatory consequence in one effect. Both decline when their consequence declines, exactly as the existing template does, so no card is promoted on an unreadable half.
items.patch:
--- a/src/cards/parse.ts
+++ b/src/cards/parse.ts
@@ -624,6 +624,18 @@
   { re: /^you may pay (\{[^ ]+\})\. if you do, (.+?)\.?$/i, make: (m, useRegistry) => { const then = parseEffects(m[2], useRegistry); if (then.some(e => e.op === 'unknown')) return null; return [{ op: 'optional-pay', mana: parseManaCost(m[1])!, then }]; } },
+  // CR 603.12 — "you may pay {m}. When you do, <X>": the payment is an action and <X> is a REFLEXIVE trigger, put on
+  // the stack (and targeted) only if the payment was actually made. Same gate as the template above, different
+  // timing, so the reflexive goes INSIDE `then` rather than beside it: one prompt, and a shape render.ts prints.
+  // Declines with its consequence, like every paragraph template here (Sparktongue Dragon, Ty Lee, Snaremaster
+  // Sprite, Halana, Kessig Ranger — 62 printings).
+  { re: /^you may pay (\{[^ ]+\})\. when you do, (.+?)\.?$/i, make: (m, useRegistry) => { const eff = parseEffects(m[2], useRegistry); if (eff.some(e => e.op === 'unknown')) return null; const mana = parseManaCost(m[1]); if (!mana || mana.x > 0) return null; return [{ op: 'optional-pay', mana, then: [{ op: 'reflexive', when: 'you-do', effects: eff }] }]; } },
+  // CR 118.12 — "you may pay {m}. If you don't, <X>": <X> is MANDATORY unless the payment is made. Claiming the
+  // payment half alone inverts the card (paying becomes purely punitive and <X> is dropped), so the pair has to be
+  // one `unless-pays` (Knight of the Mists, Rohgahh of Kher Keep, Chaos Spewer, Koya, Death from Above).
+  { re: /^you may pay (\{[^ ]+\})\. if you don't, (.+?)\.?$/i, make: (m, useRegistry) => { const otherwise = parseEffects(m[2], useRegistry); if (otherwise.some(e => e.op === 'unknown')) return null; const mana = parseManaCost(m[1]); if (!mana || mana.x > 0) return null; return [{ op: 'unless-pays', who: 'you', cost: { mana }, otherwise }]; } },

items.why: `case 'optional-pay'` unconditionally prints "…. if you do, " + renderEffects(then). With `then: []` that is a dangling "if you do, ." — verified by calling renderEffect on the shape the reviewed draft emitted ("you may pay {2}{R}. if you do, "). render.ts is what scoreCard / scoreClaimedLine read, so any card carrying that shape is scored against a sentence it does not print. The decline keeps the shape out of the pool (pinned pool-wide in test/parser-generic-you-may-pay.test.ts); this patch is what would have to land first if an empty `then` were ever to be emitted deliberately.
items.patch:
--- a/src/cards/render.ts
+++ b/src/cards/render.ts
@@
-    case 'optional-pay': return `${ctx.you} may pay ${renderMana(x.mana as ManaCost)}. if you do, ${renderEffects(x.then as Effect[], ctx)}`;
+    // An empty `then` is "pay this, and paying it does nothing by itself" — the sentence has no "if you do" half, so
+    // printing one leaves a dangling "if you do, ." that scoreClaimedLine then scores the card against.
+    case 'optional-pay': return (x.then as Effect[]).length
+      ? `${ctx.you} may pay ${renderMana(x.mana as ManaCost)}. if you do, ${renderEffects(x.then as Effect[], ctx)}`
+      : `${ctx.you} may pay ${renderMana(x.mana as ManaCost)}`;

items.why: The ONLY reason the 69 "(same unparsed lines)" cards keep their line in def.unparsed, and the only way this construct could ever be claimed as a UNIT. CR 205.1b's retention clause is its own SENTENCE, and parse.ts splits a paragraph into sentences before any rule runs, so `becomeRule` (src/cards/rules/layers.ts) never sees the retention and must decline the animation it qualifies: read alone, "becomes a 4/4 blue and black Shark creature" SETS a creature subtype, which CR 205.1a makes a replacement while this engine's layers only union. The registry cannot bridge the two sentences either — LINE_RULES is the only hook that sees a whole line, and it is unreachable for these cards (the triggered, planeswalker-loyalty, spell and cost-parsing-activated branches of the parseCard line loop all `continue` above it). Folding the clause back into the sentence it qualifies, in CR 205.1b's own words, makes becomeRule's `stripAddition` see the retention and lets the man-land cycle (Restless *, Creeping Tar Pit, Celestial Colonnade, Lumbering Falls, Hissing Quagmire, Needle Spires, Stirring Wildwood, Shambling Vent, Mishra's Factory/Foundry, Skarrg/Clan Guildmage, Avalanche Caller, Woodwraith Corrupter, …) parse for real. The phrase must go BEFORE the duration tail, because becomeRule strips " until end of turn" first and ADDITION_RE is anchored at end-of-string; "until your next turn" is deliberately NOT folded, because `become` has no duration for it and that wording must stay declined. Not made here: parse.ts is off-limits to a parser rule family.

Blockers 1, 2 and 3 (Reaper's Talisman, Spiked Ripsaw, The Spear of Leonidas; also Strength-Testing Hammer, which the review did not list). parseEffectSentence (parse.ts:841-842) rewrites a sentence-leading "it" / "that creature" / "that permanent" to `~` — the SOURCE — unless an earlier sentence of the same paragraph set `antecedent`; a trigger body's FIRST sentence never has one. Printed "it" under "Whenever equipped creature attacks" is the trigger's object (CR 608.2f, 702.6a). game.ts:1911-1913 pumpTargets resolves target 'self' to the source permanent, so the EQUIPMENT gains the keyword. The parser already owns the correct machinery: composition.ts's `thatobj` marker -> { target: 'that' } (composition.ts:475 for "gains <kw> until end of turn", :476 for "gets +X/+Y"), and triggerBody prepends { op:'bind', as:'that', from:'triggering' } as soon as an effect mentions `that`. Only the gate is wrong. Two hunks: (a) the trigger branch, beside the identical repair it already does for "on it"; (b) the modal-bullet branch, which parses a `• ` line with no frame at all, so The Spear of Leonidas's "• Bull Rush — It gains double strike until end of turn." is not reached by (a). Measured separately because (a)'s guard also covers every other non-self filtered trigger head and (b) changes how every split-mode bullet is parsed.

Blocker 4 (Staff of Titania). tokenEffect (parse.ts:733-747) special-cases only 'artifact' and 'enchantment' as type words and pushes every other descriptor into `subtypes`, so "create a 1/1 green Forest Dryad land creature token" comes out { types: ['Creature'], subtypes: ['Forest','Dryad','Land'] }: not a land (CR 305.6 — no intrinsic {G} from the Forest subtype) and carrying a bogus subtype "Land" that is not a key of SUBTYPE_KIND (src/cards/subtype-vocab.ts, CR 111.4). 'Land' is already a member of CardType (src/cards/types.ts:7). Independently confirmed by `forge:diff --changed`, token-shape: "Staff of Titania — ours: 1/1 G Creature Dryad Forest Land / forge: 1/1 G Creature Land Dryad Forest". A one-line change, but it moves every "land creature token" line in the pool, so it belongs to a measured core slice.

`Max speed` is listed in ABILITY_WORD_RE, whose contract is CR 207.2c (an ability word has no rules meaning, so the parser strips it). "Max speed — <ability>" is not an ability word: it gates the ability on its controller having speed 4. Stripping it leaves the ability ALWAYS ON — Muraganda Raceway parses an unconditional second mana ability ({T}: Add {C}{C}), Vnwxt, Verbose Host an unconditional draw replacement, Racers' Scoreboard an unconditional {1} cost reduction. Measured over the whole pool: ALL 23 cards whose only unparsed line is "Start your engines!" carry a `Max speed —` line, so claiming the construct in the registry would flip exactly those cards to fullyParsed while every one simulates a strictly stronger card than the one printed. Removing the ABILITY_WORD_RE entry alone is not enough: FLAVOUR_PREFIX_RE then matches "Max speed — {T}: …" and strips it anyway, so both regexes need the guard. With both hunks the line falls through to the static ladder and stays unparsed (honest, and ~40 cards lose a line of coverage) until the engine has a max-speed condition to gate on. This is a parse.ts-side normalisation change, so PARSER_VERSION (src/cards/parse.ts:46, currently 5) must be bumped and parse:accept run by whoever makes it. NOT made here.

items.why: A built-in trigger head shadows the CR-correct one and must be removed/re-ordered. parse.ts has TWO rules for "Whenever you attack": line 1344 `{ on: 'attacks', self: false }` (queued once per DECLARED ATTACKER by game.ts:queueTriggers) and line 1361 `{ on: 'you-attack' }` (queued once per combat, `if (s.attackers.length)`), and the first one wins, so line 1361 is dead code for the bare spelling. CR 508.1: attackers are declared by a single turn-based action, so "Whenever you attack" triggers exactly once. Measured on the pool: all 99 printed "Whenever you attack," abilities parse to the per-attacker event, 15 of them on cards the parser reports fullyParsed (Leader's Talent, Boggart Prankster, Fire Navy Trebuchet, Kithkin Brinefarer, ...). This is why the generic-whenever-more family declines "Whenever one or more creatures you control attack" even though `you-attack` states it exactly: emitting the correct event from a rule would make the same printed ability mean two different things depending on which spelling a card carries. Expect parse:diff to move the cards whose abilities change event kind; accept deliberately.
cards: Storm the Vault // Vault of Catlacan

items.why: `triggerBody` gives EVERY non-self trigger body the frame — `withFrame(!selfEv, ...)` plus a `{ op: 'bind', as: 'that', from: 'triggering' }` prefix — but game.ts sets `item.triggeringId` only from `triggerCtx.obj`, and the objectless events (you-attack, upkeep, end-step, draw-step, combat-begin, life-gain, life-loss-opponent, end-of-turn) carry no object. The bind then binds nothing and every `that` / `those` in the body resolves to the empty set: the ability resolves, touches nothing, and the card still reports fullyParsed. Verified in a real game: parsing Angelic Guardian's head as `you-attack` gives `[bind that from triggering, grant-keyword those indestructible eot]`; the log shows the trigger firing and resolving and the attacker still dies to a Lightning Bolt. 33 abilities in the pool already sit on an objectless event with that prefix (most are harmless because a later effect rebinds the frame from its own targets). This is the second reason the family declines the one CR-exact wording it found. CAVEAT for the core slice: a body may legitimately bind the frame from its OWN earlier effect ("...put a +1/+1 counter on target creature you control. It gains lifelink"), so the patch must be validated with parse:diff before acceptance — it removes only the INCOMING binding.
cards: Storm the Vault // Vault of Catlacan

items.why: BLOCKER 2. `/^whenever you attack$/` at parse.ts:1344 answers {on:'attacks', self:false} and shadows the correct `/^whenever you attack(?: a player)?$/` -> {on:'you-attack'} at parse.ts:1361. The engine queues 'attacks' once per attacker (game.ts:220, :2270, :2408) and 'you-attack' once as attackers are declared (:2275), so the shadowed head fires N times in an N-attacker combat. CR 508.1 / 603.2; Forge encodes it `T:Mode$ AttackersDeclared | AttackingPlayer$ You` and forge:diff already flags it (trigger-kind calibration 4/4 parser-wrong). Pre-existing: 16 already-fully-parsed cards carry it (Battlesong Berserker, Temmet, Razorkin Hordecaller, …), so the delete needs its own parse:diff group read; the family declines the wording meanwhile so Labyrinth Adversary is not the first card made simulable with it.
cards: Casal, Lurkwood Pathfinder // Casal, Pathbreaker Owlbear

items.why: CORRECTED RECORD (this is the fix for the review's major finding; the first pass's member list was wrong). "<an optional action>. If you don't, <Y>" is a two-sentence composition, and the only place parse.ts joins two sentences is its own PARAGRAPH_RULES table — a built-in a rule family may fill the slots of but not extend. The template below is what such an entry would look like. MEASURED, not asserted: applied to the normalised paragraph body of all 79 printed lines of the construct in the pool (trigger line past its head and intervening "if"; loyalty ability past "N:"; spell paragraph whole), with the cost slot run through the real parseCostPhrase and the else slot through parseEffects, it MATCHES 17 lines and CLAIMS exactly ONE — Lim-Dûl's Paladin, "At the beginning of your upkeep, you may discard a card. If you don't, sacrifice ~ and draw a card." (the first pass also misspelled the name as "Lim-Dul's"). Of the eight further cards the first pass named as covered: Imprison (both lines) and Koya, Death from Above NEVER MATCH — "If you do," is the sentence after Imprison's optional pay, and Koya's optional pay sits inside a delayed trigger ("At the beginning of the next end step, …"), so the `^` anchor cannot start there; Songbirds' Blessing never matches either, and NOT for the reason the first pass gave — its body begins "reveal cards from the top of your library …", so `^you may` fails one stage EARLIER than parseCostPhrase, and it is not the case the trailing `(?=$| [A-Z~])` sentence stop protects. Chaos Spewer, Knight of the Mists, Yawgmoth Demon and Rohgahh of Kher Keep do match and then decline in the `otherwise` slot ("blight 2" has no op; "destroy target Knight" is a bare creature-subtype target word; "tap ~ and it deals 2 damage to you" is an "and"-joined two-clause sentence; Rohgahh's else fails on both counts). Devouring Sugarmaw // Have for Dinner matches and declines in the COST slot ("sacrifice an artifact, enchantment, or token" — parseFilterWords has no comma list). Structural consequence: PARAGRAPH_RULES only ever match at the front of what is left of a paragraph (parseParagraph consumes a template's m[0] and retries at `^`), so any member whose optional action is not the paragraph's FIRST sentence is out of reach of a paragraph template altogether — 62 of the 79 lines. RECOMMENDATION: do not make this core change yet. At one claimed card it is not earned; the else-branch and cost-slot vocabulary named in openIssues has to land first, and even then it reaches only the 17 head-of-paragraph members. The wording stays declined either way, because no rule family can add the entry.

--- a/src/cards/parse.ts
+++ b/src/cards/parse.ts
@@ -625,6 +625,17 @@ const PARAGRAPH_RULES: { re: RegExp; make: (m: RegExpMatchArray, useRegistry: boo
   { re: /^discard a card\. if you do, draw a card\.?/i, make: () => [{ op: 'loot', draw: 1, discard: 1, discardFirst: true }] },
+  // "You may <pay a cost>. If you don't, Y" — the two-sentence spelling of "… unless you pay <cost>" (CR 118.12),
+  // and so exactly `unless-pays`. It must sit BELOW `optional-pay` / `optional-then`: "If you do," is a prefix of
+  // neither, but Imprison ("you may pay {1}. If you do, counter that ability. If you don't, destroy ~.") is offered
+  // to `optional-pay` first and only reaches here after that declines — and then this template declines too, because
+  // it requires "If you don't," to follow the optional action directly. The `[^.{]` first character keeps the
+  // non-mana branch off "pay {2}" (the mana branch above it owns that), and the `(?=$| [A-Z~])` stop ends Y at its
+  // own sentence. MEASURED yield over the pool: 17 lines match, 1 is claimed (Lim-Dûl's Paladin) — the other 16
+  // decline in a slot, and 62 further lines of the construct never match because their optional action is not the
+  // paragraph's first sentence. Not worth landing until the openIssues vocabulary does.
+  { re: /^you may (?:pay (\{[^ ]+\})|([^.{][^.]*?))\. if you don't, ([^.]+)\.?(?=$| [A-Z~])/i, make: (m, useRegistry) => {
+    const cost = m[1] ? { mana: parseManaCost(m[1])! } : parseCostPhrase(m[2], useRegistry); if (!cost) return null;
+    const otherwise = parseEffects(m[3], useRegistry); if (otherwise.some(e => e.op === 'unknown')) return null;
+    return [{ op: 'unless-pays', who: 'you', cost, otherwise }]; } },
   // Y is captured greedily up to the next period: under /i the old lazy `([^.]+?)\.?(?=$| [A-Z~])` stopped at the
   // first space ("draw" of "draw two cards"), so the template declined on nearly every real card (PARSER_VERSION 2).
   { re: /^you may ([^.]+?)\. if you do, ([^.]+)\.?(?=$| [A-Z~])/i, make: (m, useRegistry) => { const first = parseEffects(m[1], useRegistry); const then = parseEffects(m[2], useRegistry); if (first.some(e => e.op === 'unknown') || then.some(e => e.op === 'unknown')) return null; return [{ op: 'optional-then', first, then }]; } },

items.why: ROUND 2 (supersedes the round-1 you-may-pay-2 records): The construct's whole difficulty is the sentence AFTER the payment, and only a PARAGRAPH template sees it. parse.ts already owns "you may pay {m}. If you do, <body>" as one paragraph (line 624); the "When you do" sibling has no template, so the payment sentence falls through to the sentence ladder alone, where no rule can tell the three printed continuations apart. Anchoring the new template at $ makes a rider printed after the reflexive (Terror of Towashi's "It's a Phyrexian...", Spined Tyrranax's "That creature gains trample...") part of the body, so a body that does not fully parse declines the whole pair — which is exactly the gate review major 4 asked for, keyed on the right property. With this in place the four correct cards (Sparktongue Dragon, Thousand Moons Crackshot, Icewrought Sentry, Evereth) parse with no over-claim, the 16 "If you do" cards keep their honest unknowns, and no `may` is wrapped around the payment (a paragraph template's effects are not re-wrapped).

   { re: /^you may pay (\{[^ ]+\})\. if you do, (.+?)\.?$/i, make: (m, useRegistry) => { const then = parseEffects(m[2], useRegistry); if (then.some(e => e.op === 'unknown')) return null; return [{ op: 'optional-pay', mana: parseManaCost(m[1])!, then }]; } },
+  // "You may pay {2}{R}. When you do, <body>." (Sparktongue Dragon) — the sibling of the template above, and the one
+  // shape a sentence rule cannot answer: an EffectRule sees ONE sentence, and "When you do" / "If you do" / "If you
+  // don't" are three different meanings behind an identical payment sentence. CR 603.12 makes the second sentence a
+  // REFLEXIVE trigger that is put on the stack from the resolving ability and chooses its targets there, so the body
+  // does NOT go in `then`. `$` is load-bearing: a rider printed after the reflexive is part of m[2], so a body that
+  // does not fully parse declines the pair instead of hoisting the rider out of the ability it belongs to.
+  { re: /^you may pay ((?:\{[^{}]+\})+)\. when you do, (.+?)\.?$/i, make: (m, useRegistry) => { const mana = parseManaCost(m[1]); const then = parseEffects(m[2], useRegistry); if (!mana || !then.length || then.some(e => e.op === 'unknown')) return null; return [{ op: 'optional-pay', mana, then: [] }, { op: 'reflexive', when: 'you-do', effects: then }]; } },
   { re: /^discard a card\. if you do, draw a card\.?/i, make: () => [{ op: 'loot', draw: 1, discard: 1, discardFirst: true }] },

items.why: ROUND 2 (supersedes the round-1 you-may-pay-2 records): Review major 3, unchanged from round 1 and still core-only: the registry hook in parseEffectSentence wraps EVERY claim of a "You may ..." sentence in a `may`, without the guard its own built-in branch applies twelve lines above, so an op that already carries its own yes/no ask is asked twice — and the outer ask is offered even when the inner one could not succeed. A rule cannot opt out: it never sees the "you may ". `optional-pay` is such an op (game.ts's `case 'optional-pay'` asks `<name>: pay <mana>?`), so it belongs in the PERMISSION_OPS set, which already means "the op's own template reads the 'you may'". No built-in EFFECT_RULE emits `optional-pay` (only the paragraph template at 624 and the extort line at 1960, neither of which goes through this hook), so the set change moves no existing parse.
cards: Casal, Lurkwood Pathfinder // Casal, Pathbreaker Owlbear

items.why: ROUND 2 (supersedes the round-1 you-may-pay-2 records): render.ts:833 appends ". if you do, <then>" unconditionally, so an `optional-pay` with an empty `then` — which is what the paragraph template in the first patch emits, the payment and a separate reflexive — renders as "you may pay {2}{R}. if you do, ." Reported in round 1, still open, and it becomes visible the moment the first patch lands.
items.patch:
--- a/src/cards/render.ts
+++ b/src/cards/render.ts
@@ -831,7 +831,8 @@
-    case 'optional-pay': return `${ctx.you} may pay ${renderMana(x.mana as ManaCost)}. if you do, ${renderEffects(x.then as Effect[], ctx)}`;
+    // an empty `then` is the printed "You may pay {2}{R}." whose consequence is a separate reflexive trigger (CR
+    // 603.12), not a missing half: rendering ". if you do, " after it prints a dangling clause.
+    case 'optional-pay': { const pay = `${ctx.you} may pay ${renderMana(x.mana as ManaCost)}`; const then = x.then as Effect[]; return then.length ? `${pay}. if you do, ${renderEffects(then, ctx)}` : pay; }

items.why: ROUND 2: ONE hunk in amountFor fixes BOTH blockers. "its power" / "its toughness" / "its mana value" are an OBJECT's characteristics (CR 208.1), read as last known information when the object has died (CR 608.2h), so a sentence whose SUBJECT is a player can never be the antecedent of "its". amountFor has two subject heuristics and neither excludes a player subject: (1) `aboutTarget` fires on any base that starts "target ", so Dying Wish's "target player loses X life and you gain X life" binds X to {prop:'power',of:'target:0'} — the target player, which src/engine/refs.ts resolves to no object, so characteristics.ts reads 0 and the drain is always 0; (2) `aboutSelf` fires on any base containing a bare `~`, and parse.ts has already rewritten Banewasp Affliction's leading possessive "that creature's controller" to "~'s controller", so X binds to {prop:'toughness',of:'self'} — the Aura, an Enchantment - Aura with null P/T, so the loss is always 0. With the guard in, both fall through to the generic amount path: Dying Wish gets the built-in phrase {count:'power-of-that'} and Banewasp gets propOf's {prop:'toughness',of:'that'} — in both cases the triggering object that triggerBody() binds, i.e. the creature that died. Death Watch ("its controller loses life equal to its power and you gain life equal to its toughness") already emits exactly those two shapes, so this is the binding the vocabulary already has. The third `else if (/\btarget\b/i.test(base)) return null;` must also skip a player subject, otherwise Dying Wish goes from wrong to declined instead of right. Verify with `npm run parse:diff` (the "X is its …" groups) and re-run test/parser-composition.test.ts.

ROUND 2: Secondary / contributing cause of blocker 2, recorded because it is the case the brief names verbatim ("a pronoun parse.ts rewrites before any rule runs"). parseEffectSentence's leading-pronoun rewrite uses `\b` after "that creature", and `\b` matches in front of the apostrophe, so the POSSESSIVE "that creature's controller loses life equal to its toughness" becomes "~'s controller loses …" before any registry rule can see it. That injected `~` is what trips composition's `aboutSelf` test. The narrow fix is below, but it is riskier than the composition.ts hunk: several built-in templates accept "~'s controller" precisely because of this rewrite (parse.ts's "(?:its|~'s|that creature's|that permanent's) controller …" family, which is how Pattern of Rebirth gets its correct controller-of-that scope), so re-routing the possessive to the `thatobj` marker moves those parses too and needs its own parse:diff pass. The composition.ts hunk alone fixes both printed cards without touching any of that, so PREFER IT; this entry is the alternative, not an additional requirement.
items.patch:
--- a/src/cards/parse.ts
+++ b/src/cards/parse.ts
@@ export function parseEffectSentence(sentence: string, useRegistry = true): Effect
-  if (antecedent && /^(?:it|that creature|that permanent) (?:gains?|gets?|has base power|loses?|becomes?|deals?) /i.test(s)) s = s.replace(/^(?:it|that creature|that permanent)\b/i, 'thatobj');   // 9.1: becomes / deals too (layers, Wolf Strike)
-  else s = s.replace(/^(?:it|that creature|that permanent|this creature|this permanent)\b/i, '~');
+  if (antecedent && /^(?:it|that creature|that permanent) (?:gains?|gets?|has base power|loses?|becomes?|deals?) /i.test(s)) s = s.replace(/^(?:it|that creature|that permanent)\b/i, 'thatobj');   // 9.1: becomes / deals too (layers, Wolf Strike)
+  // `\b` matches in front of an apostrophe, so a leading POSSESSIVE ("that creature's controller …") used to become
+  // "~'s controller …" — the source — and any "its power/toughness" in the same sentence then read the source's
+  // (Banewasp Affliction, always 0). A possessive subject is the frame's object, never `~`.
+  else if (antecedent && /^(?:it|that creature|that permanent)'s /i.test(s)) s = s.replace(/^(?:it|that creature|that permanent)(?='s )/i, 'thatobj');
+  else s = s.replace(/^(?:it|that creature|that permanent|this creature|this permanent)\b/i, '~');
